questions.text: In an audio encoder → projector → language model architecture, what is the projector’s main role?

options.A: Convert the language model’s text output into waveform samples.
options.B: Assign speaker identities to every segment before encoding.
options.C: Map audio-encoder features into the language model’s embedding space.
options.D: Compute word error rate between the model output and a reference.

questions.explanation: The projector bridges the audio encoder’s feature representation and the language model’s input embedding space.

questions.text: An audio-language model has strong aggregate QA accuracy. Your task requires comparing two clips. What evaluation best establishes whether it fits your task?

options.A: Evaluate a representative multi-audio comparison subset separately.
options.B: Use aggregate accuracy as proof of equal performance across categories.
options.C: Evaluate only single-clip speech transcription questions.
options.D: Choose the largest model without evaluating clip comparisons.

questions.explanation: Aggregate results can hide category-specific weaknesses. Direct multi-audio comparison evaluation tests the capability the deployment actually needs.

questions.text: AudioProjector applies Linear(1280, 4096), GELU, then Linear(4096, 4096) to the last dimension. For input shape (2, 50, 1280), what is the output shape?
questions.explanation: The linear layers transform only the last feature dimension; the batch size 2 and sequence length 50 remain unchanged.
